findings.title: Weak encryption algorithm: 3DES
findings.description: 3DES has a 64-bit block size and is deprecated; it is vulnerable to birthday attacks such as Sweet32.

findings.title: Weak hash algorithm: MD5
findings.description: MD5 is cryptographically broken and should not be used for integrity protection.

findings.title: Weak Diffie-Hellman group: DH group 2
findings.description: DH group 2 uses a 1024-bit modulus, which is below current minimum recommendations.

findings.title: Legacy protocol version: IKEv1
findings.description: IKEv1 is deprecated in favour of IKEv2, which has stronger defaults and better resistance to attacks.

findings.title: IKEv1 Aggressive Mode in use
findings.description: Aggressive Mode exposes a hash of the pre-shared key that can be captured and cracked offline.

findings.title: Pre-Shared Key authentication
findings.description: Pre-shared keys are weaker than certificate-based authentication and are hard to rotate safely.

findings.title: Perfect Forward Secrecy disabled
findings.description: Without PFS, compromise of one key can expose traffic from other sessions.

findings.title: Identity sent in clear
findings.description: Peer identity is transmitted unencrypted during the handshake and can be observed by an eavesdropper.

findings.title: AES-256-CBC used instead of an AEAD cipher
findings.description: AES-256-CBC is acceptable but AES-GCM is preferred because it provides authenticated encryption.

findings.title: SA lifetime over 86400 seconds
findings.description: Lifetime of 100000 seconds exceeds the recommended 86400-second maximum, increasing key exposure time.
